From dfbc282c2e16cd6044e4181f150dbd1e2224eaa7 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Masatake YAMATO <yamato@redhat.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2014 11:49:17 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] check multiple parser methods are not defined in a parser

This fixes a bug introduced in be4a2117494ce73750cec3fd3c7cb4a60e722bcf.

The old commit(be4a21) checked only the case that allparser, parser2 and parser_with_gc
were not set but didn't check more than one were set. This patch checks this case, too.

Signed-off-by: Masatake YAMATO <yamato@redhat.com>

diff --git a/parse.c b/parse.c
index 557228d1d..2ae586ea0 100644
--- a/parse.c
+++ b/parse.c
@@ -969,7 +969,7 @@ extern void initializeParsing (void)
 				accepted = TRUE;
 #endif
 			}
-			else if ((def->parser == NULL)  &&  (def->parser2 == NULL) && (def->parser_with_gc == NULL))
+			else if (((!!def->parser) + (!!def->parser2) + (!!def->parser_with_gc)) != 1)
 				error (FATAL,
 		"%s parser definition must define one and only one parsing routine\n",
 					   def->name);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `parse.c`**
- The condition that checks for parser definitions has been modified. 
- The original condition checked if all three parser methods (`parser`, `parser2`, and `parser_with_gc`) were `NULL`. 
- The new condition checks if exactly one of the parser methods is defined by using the expression `((!!def->parser) + (!!def->parser2) + (!!def->parser_with_gc)) != 1`. This ensures that if more than one parser method is defined, an error is raised.

### Relationships
- The modification in `parse.c` addresses a bug introduced in a previous commit (be4a2117494ce73750cec3fd3c7cb4a60e722bcf) that only checked if all parser methods were unset, but did not account for the scenario where multiple parser methods were defined simultaneously. The new check ensures that the parser definitions adhere to the requirement of having exactly one parser method defined, thus preventing potential conflicts or undefined behavior in the parsing logic.

```c
else if ((def->parser == NULL) && (def->parser2 == NULL) && (def->parser_with_gc == NULL))
```
Reason:
This statement only checks if all parser methods are `NULL`, allowing multiple parser methods to be defined simultaneously without raising an error. This can lead to ambiguity in which parser method should be used, resulting in potential conflicts or incorrect parsing behavior.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
else if (((!!def->parser) + (!!def->parser2) + (!!def->parser_with_gc)) != 1)
```
Reason:
This statement checks that exactly one of the parser methods (`parser`, `parser2`, or `parser_with_gc`) is defined (i.e., not `NULL`). If more than one method is defined, it raises an error, thus preventing ambiguity and ensuring that only one parser method is used, which resolves the bug.
